title: Nine Pence and Eleven Minutes
subtitle: 酒饮与社交 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 酒饮与社交（生活与学习·饮食与社交）
meta: 主题语境：酒饮与社交（生活与学习·饮食与社交）　|　核心词汇：beer　|　正文 323 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 beer 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 my uncle bought ① a beer for a man he had never met and said the buying was the whole of the friendship. The ② beer, meaning the glass and not the evening, cost nine pence and lasted eleven minutes; a beer, he said, is the only purchase that is measured by who was standing there.

Every ③ beer in that town was the same colour, and the ④ beer on the table, meaning the one nobody had paid for and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever remembered. A beer, my grandmother said, is nine parts company and one part somebody willing to listen; my uncle said the company is the part you pay for.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ beer was the whole of the debt, meaning the obligation and not the glass. The ⑥ beer, meaning the favour owed and not any of that, is the only thing in a town that is repaid without anybody asking; a beer, she said, is either something you drink or the only word that means both a glass and an obligation. He said the obligation is the part that lasts.

By 1967 the ⑦ beer had become a photograph in a window, and the window had become an argument about the price. The ⑧ beer of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in May, was nine pence and eleven years of standing there; a beer, he said, is either the glass on the table or the reason you know who was in the room. She said knowing was the part that mattered.

The ⑨ beer I remember is the one on the table, which nobody had paid for and everybody had drunk. A ⑩ beer, my grandmother said in 1969, is the only thing that improves by being owed; every beer, she said, is an obligation that has agreed to look like a glass. He said the obligation was never in the glass.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 啤酒（一杯啤酒）
B. n. 啤酒（指那杯酒，与那个夜晚相对）
C. 固定搭配：buy a beer 买一杯啤酒
D. n. 啤酒（指那个镇上每一杯）
E. n. 啤酒（指桌上那一杯）
F. n. 人情；欠下的人情债（指那份义务）
G. n. 人情债（抽象：那种该还的人情）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a beer for a man he had never met
The beer, meaning the glass and not the evening
beer was the whole of the debt
The beer, meaning the favour owed
the beer had become a photograph in a window
The beer of the whole thing

answers.why: buy a beer 意为“买一杯啤酒”，1954 年叔叔给一个素不相识的人买了一杯啤酒。
beer 意为“啤酒”，指那杯酒而不是那个夜晚，它花了九便士，喝了十一分钟。
beer 指那个镇上每一杯啤酒，每一杯都是同一个颜色。
beer 指桌上那一杯（没人付钱的那杯），是唯一有人记得的。
beer 意为“人情、欠下的人情债”，指那份义务，母亲说 beer 就是那笔债的全部。
beer 为抽象用法，指该还的那份人情，是镇上唯一不用人开口就会还的东西。
beer 意为“啤酒”，到 1967 年这个 beer 成了橱窗里的一张照片。
beer 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，叔叔五月写道，整件事权衡下来是九便士和站在那里的十一年。
beer 意为“啤酒”，我记得的是桌上那一杯，没人付过钱，人人都喝过。
beer 为抽象总称，祖母说啤酒是唯一会因为欠着而变好的东西。

The beer on the table, meaning the one nobody had paid for and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever remembered.
My mother said beer was the whole of the debt, meaning the obligation and not the glass.
